topic: Performance Optimization: Reducing Procedure Call Overhead
explanation: Procedure calls introduce overhead due to function prologue/epilogue, stack manipulation, and branch prediction mis-predictions.  In performance-critical sections, this overhead can significantly impact execution time. Reducing procedure calls improves performance by minimizing these overheads, allowing for more efficient instruction execution and better utilization of the processor pipeline.
syntax: Replacing function calls with inline code or using loop unrolling to reduce function call frequency within loops.
example_explanation: The example illustrates the performance optimization technique of reducing procedure calls. The original code calls `get_vec_element` repeatedly within a loop.  Each call incurs overhead. The optimized code replaces the function call with its inline equivalent. This eliminates the function call overhead, leading to faster execution.  This directly demonstrates the impact of procedure call overhead on performance by reducing the number of function calls and minimizing context switching and branch prediction inefficiencies.  In real-world scenarios, the improvement might be further enhanced by compiler optimizations applied to the inline code.
